# Respectful participation

CSCI 3141 brings together students with different backgrounds, interests, and
experience in statistics and programming. Everyone should be able to ask a
question, explain an idea, and learn from a mistake without being demeaned.
These expectations apply in class, in the course Microsoft Teams space, during
portfolio presentations, and when discussing the published course materials.

## Discuss ideas with care

Good data science depends on questioning assumptions and checking evidence.
Disagreement is part of that work. Keep it focused on the analysis and explain
your reasoning.

- Critique a method, claim, or interpretation without attacking the person
  presenting it.
- Give others room to ask questions and contribute. Do not assume that everyone
  has the same familiarity with R, Python, Git, or the subject of a dataset.
- When you challenge a result, identify the relevant data, definition, code
  step, or source so the question can be examined together.
- Keep academic disagreement civil and free from harassment or discrimination.

If a document format, tool, or classroom practice creates a barrier to
participation, raise it with the instructor. Accommodation information is
private and follows the approved university process.

## Respect classmates' work and privacy

Discussing concepts is encouraged, while submitted work must show each
student's own understanding. Follow the written assessment instructions before
sharing code, answers, analysis files, or solution steps.

Keep assessed work private until its submission deadline has passed and the
instructor opens sharing. Once work is released for presentation, discuss it
respectfully and preserve its attribution. Publication of course materials does
not grant permission to redistribute another student's work.

Grades, feedback, personal circumstances, and instructor-marked private
materials belong in private channels. Do not record, photograph, stream, or
redistribute a class without written permission or an accommodation. The
[portfolio guide](../README.md#your-data-science-portfolio) explains the
submission and release workflow.

## Raise a concern privately

Contact Prof. Gabriel Spadon at [spadon@dal.ca](mailto:spadon@dal.ca) about an
individual concern. Enrolled students should use their Dalhousie email.
Describe what happened and the context needed to understand it without
repeating personal information in a public issue or class-wide message.

The [syllabus](../assets/planning/syllabus.pdf) sets the course requirements and
links the university's conduct, accessibility, academic integrity, and support
resources. Those policies and processes govern how concerns are addressed;
use the university routes in the syllabus when another contact is appropriate.
